findings.title: Reject unsupported actor values instead of silently coercing them.
findings.rationale:
actor: any allows objects and nullish values. String(actor) stores `{ id: "alice" } as "[object Object]", and stores null or undefined` as literal actor names. This loses actor identity and can corrupt audit attribution. Some objects can also make String() throw before the event is appended.

Keep actor string-only, or validate documented actor shapes and reject unsupported values.

Proposed fix

-export function record(event: string, actor: any): void { -  events.push({ event, actor: String(actor) }); +export function record(event: string, actor: string): void { +  events.push({ event, actor }); }
